title: An observed-basis refusal on a bound criterion names a valid verification citation as if it were at fault
outcome: An observed-basis refusal on a bound criterion names a valid verification citation as if it were at fault
acceptance: The evaluate refusal texts for a bound criterion state what an admissible pass is: basis observed, every citation a passed host-minted verification of the bound kind cited by its full record id; a test pins the text

When evaluate refuses a pass on a criterion bound to a check kind because its basis is not observed (observed_basis_required), the refusal's message and cause say the basis is wrong and name no cited record as the offending one, or name every citation as unchecked; a test submits a pass with a judgment basis whose first citation is a valid passed verification of the bound kind and asserts the refusal does not attribute the failure to that citation

completion.summary: A pass on a criterion bound to a check with a basis other than observed (observed_basis_required), and an asserted pass under an observed mechanical policy (observed_policy_required), are now refused with an empty cause citation and no position. The basis is the fault, so a valid passed verification is never named as the refused record. Every other citation refusal still names the record at fault; codes, exits, reason text, mismatches and check order are unchanged. The read_run_evidence remedy states the admissible pass for a bound criterion. Tests cover the wrong basis with a valid verification first, note-only, an observed pass mixing a note in either order, a non-pass verdict, the observed-policy case, and the MCP transport. Landed 7c4c694 after two rounds (round 1 had no Claude because of TermAl phantoms; round 2 clean). Full gate test-27c956d1 passed 9/9; ready on 4 stores; the independent evaluation passed 2/2.
